html:
Sālote Tupou III was queen of Tonga from 1918 to 1965, one of the longest reigns of the century. She healed old church and chiefly feuds and brought schools and health care to the islands.

She was also a poet and composer, and her songs and dances are still performed.

The wider world met her in 1953, at the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II in London, when she rode through heavy rain in an open carriage and waved to the crowds. She upheld the constitution of her ancestor George Tupou I.
